The story relies on several overused tropes and expressions—or clichés—commonly found in dramatic reconciliation scenes. These include the setting of a rainy train station café, the awkward hesitation over whether to hug, the nervous habit of stirring a coffee that is already stirred, keeping a jacket on to signal a reluctance to stay (and unzipping it as emotional walls come down), and predictable dialogue exchanges such as "You look good" / "You're still a bad liar." Because it uses so many familiar, predictable elements, it is not entirely free of clichés.
